spec.title: APP-CLEAN campaign v0.1 — the clean user-application subsystem

status.comment: Closed 2026-10-31: P1–P6 landed, gate green, MT-04/MT-05 await the owner's native runs.

p.mandate: «возьми процесс в свои руки и доведи работу. Можешь использовать Opus 5.5 в качестве исполнителя-субагента, когда нужно.» «почисти всё от слопа, сделай пожалуйста красивое чистое решение, которое удовлетворяет изначальным желаниям. Без ерунды типа ACID-транзакций бесконечной надежности.» «и спецификацию от ерунды тоже стоит почистить». The original wishes are the mandates recorded in the archived plan: declared platform/architecture/installer options with shell, archive, EXE, MSI methods, forced operations and hooks, authored launchers, slot alternatives with one global and distinct per-shell choices, direct native launch, the Vim bridge; sources fetched by URL or local path with platform-specific sh / PowerShell recipes; several storage libraries with attach, detach, inventory, unavailability and moves; portability by default; a top-level `vibe shell`.

p.baseline: Local `main` reset to `7081b2376` (installer-options model, native proxy, Phase 0R fixes; +14 743 / −2 489 lines over v1.0.7). The prototype (729 commits, +354k lines) is `archive/app-overlay-prototype-2026-10`; its J/3 continuation is branch `app-publication-j3`. Nothing after v1.0.7 was ever pushed. `cargo build -p vibe-cli --bins` is green at the baseline. The contract is the rewritten `PROP-059`, which `vibe check` accepts with 0 errors. The machine has 14 GiB free on an ext4 disk with a 64 GiB warm `target/`, so packets run sequentially in this checkout, never in parallel worktrees.

p.decision-rewrite: D1 — rewrite the subsystem as the `vibe-app` library crate with thin CLI and proxy surfaces, reusing reviewed pieces of the baseline (option selection, archive extraction safety, launcher template grammar, registry resolution, Windows proxy supervision) and deleting the rest (installer child-process protocol, leases, projections, pending-removal intents, release-index distribution). Rejected: incremental refactoring of the baseline module, because its index, proxy descriptor and alternatives model already carry the prototype's shape.

p.decision-state: D2 — one index file, one `storage.toml`, library markers, directories; atomic rename only. Rejected: any journal, checkpoint, lease or recovery command (`PROP-059#decisions`).

p.decision-session: D3 — session alternatives are the `VIBE_APP_USE` environment variable read by the proxy. Rejected: per-session PATH view directories with masks (files to publish, recover and garbage-collect for a choice that is inherently process-scoped).

p.decision-recipe: D4 — source builds are a plain recipe runner inside `vibe-app`. Rejected: routing through the project Build/Package lifecycle planes, which coupled applications to project artifact records in the prototype.

p.decision-executors: D5 — the owner designated Opus 5.5 subagents as executors for this campaign; the central session owns the contract, packet authoring, every review and every commit. This is an owner override of the delegation-first GLM route for the campaign's duration.

p.phase-1: P1 — manifest model, `vibe-app` crate (settings, storage libraries, index `/3`, resolution, selection, shell / zip / tar_gz / exe / msi installers, hooks, force, install / update / uninstall, launch), CLI wiring, removal of the baseline module and the retired `application/e1` wire formats. Gate: public Linux fixtures for shell and archive install → list → run → uninstall; workspace build, tests, clippy, conform, codegen and wire-diff green.

p.phase-2: P2 — proxy binary rewrite and publication, `app use`, `app alternatives`, `VIBE_APP_USE`, `vibe shell`. Gate: public Linux fixture with two providers in one slot, global switch, two concurrent session choices, PTY shell test.

p.phase-3: P3 — `source_build` method: inputs, cache, recipe runner, offline. Gate: public Linux fixture with one locally served URL source and one package-local file.

p.phase-4: P4 — `vibe storage` list / add / attach / detach / move / gc, unavailability through launch and proxy, portability. Gate: public Linux two-library fixture per `PROP-059#acceptance`.

p.phase-5: P5 — manual tests for Windows and macOS, user documentation, the Vim bridge package refreshed against the final manifest, full `tools/self-check.sh`, health-audit entry, close-out report.

p.phase-6: P6 — project-local applications per `PROP-059#project-scope`: app dependencies in `vibe.toml` / `vibe.lock`, the project home `vibevm/vibeopt/` with the user-home layout, consent-gated materialisation on `vibe install`, home selection for `update` / `uninstall` / `app` without `-g`, two-home PATH in `vibe shell`, git ignore. Gate: public Linux fixture that installs an app into a fresh project, runs it through the project `opt/bin` inside `vibe shell`, and reinstalls it from the lockfile in a second checkout.

p.report: Commit range `6ade17d8b..a435a9abf` on local `main` (21 commits). Result against the mandate: declared platform / architecture / installer options with shell, ZIP, tar.gz, EXE, MSI and source_build; force and hooks; launchers with direct native launch; slot alternatives with one global default and a per-shell choice through `VIBE_APP_USE`; native PATH proxies; `vibe shell`; storage libraries with add / attach / detach / list / move / gc and observed availability; portability by default; project-local installs from the lockfile; the Vim bridge rebuilt on the model with source builds for Linux and macOS; the documentation site installable again. Size: `vibe-app` 5 9xx lines with tests against the prototype's 350k; durable state is one index, one `storage.toml`, directories. Verified: 1 421 `vibe-cli` tests, full gate green after removing stale fixture artifacts (AUDIT 2026-10-31-01), Vim built and relocated on this Linux host. Open: native Windows and macOS runs (MT-04, MT-05) are the owner's; publishing the Vim bridge 1.1.0 to the registry awaits the owner's word; `zap` re-declaration (B-217); agent hooks are the next campaign (owner request of 2026-10-31).

p.ledger: 2026-10-30: archive branch created, `main` reset, PROP-059 rewritten, plan authored. P1 packet dispatched. P1 reviewed and landed as 6ade17d8b + af6dfb36a: review removed a payload digest the executor had added (a full-payload hash per install and uninstall) and made `--library` on external methods a refusal; vibe-app is 3 959 lines. P2 dispatched. Owner approved project-local applications; P6 added. P2 reviewed and landed as 8211cf48b (proxy 480 lines incl. a deliberate 340-line resolution copy so the proxy depends on neither vibe-app nor vibe-core; shell 456 lines across five files). P3 dispatched. P3 reviewed and landed as the source_build commit (535-line runner; owned placement unified for archives and recipes). P4 dispatched. P4 reviewed and landed as 85d4b79b9 (storage split into mod/edit/relocate, 1 187 lines with tests). First real source build, Vim 9.2.1167 from its GitHub tarball, exposed PAX global headers; fixed in b1cbd19e1. P5 opened: the Vim bridge gained source-build options for Linux and macOS (its first build showed Vim bakes the prefix in, now wrapped), the documentation site moved to a source-build recipe with a relocatable launcher (6b315e53d), MT-04 / MT-05 written for native Windows and macOS (be0db613c), changelog and backlog recorded (6d717da40). P6 reviewed and landed: project home as the same SettingsRoot, lockfile-driven materialisation with bin-build consent, two-home shell; review fixed an exact-version key lookup the executor found in P1 (774ff9958). 2026-10-31: full self-check run; step 2 red on stale uplifted fixture libraries (B-219), green after cleanup; AUDIT section written; campaign closed.
